skill.name: dependency-management-deps-audit
skill.description: Audits project dependencies for known vulnerabilities, license conflicts, outdated packages, supply chain risks, bundle impact, and prioritized remediation options.
skill.summary: Assess dependency security, licensing, maintenance, and upgrade priorities with practical reports and workflow templates.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static detections mostly reflect benign Markdown, JavaScript templates, fixed shell expressions, and expected registry access in documentation. One low-severity network finding remains because Bundlephobia receives package names and versions. Semantic review found unsafe force-upgrade rollback guidance and unpinned CI tooling, with no malicious intent or prompt injection.

remediation.suggestion: Require consent before Bundlephobia requests, skip private packages, and document that package names and versions leave the local environment.
Remove `--force` from the default workflow. Use an isolated branch, require approval, test changes, and restore every modified manifest and lockfile.
Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs and audit tools to reviewed versions with hashes or lockfiles. Update pins through controlled review.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Force Upgrade and Incomplete Rollback
semantic_findings.description: The remediation script runs `npm audit fix --force`, which may install breaking updates and execute dependency lifecycle scripts. Its failure path reverts only `package-lock.json`.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited script directly enables forced upgrades, then restores only one file after failed tests. This leaves other modified state outside the rollback.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Executable CI Dependencies
semantic_findings.description: The CI example uses mutable action tags and installs `safety` and `license-checker` without versions. Upstream compromise or drift could execute unexpected code in CI.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow directly references major action tags and unversioned package installations. Each dependency can execute within the CI environment.

content.user_title: Audit Project Dependencies and Plan Secure Updates
content.value_statement: Dependency risks are difficult to prioritize across vulnerabilities, licenses, maintenance, and supply chain signals. This skill organizes evidence and produces practical remediation and monitoring plans.
actual_capabilities: Guides inventory of direct and transitive dependencies from common package manifests and lockfiles.
Checks packages against vulnerability sources and prioritizes findings by severity, exploit signals, and runtime exposure.
Reviews dependency licenses for compatibility, restrictions, unknown terms, and required legal review.
Ranks outdated packages by update type, age, security value, and estimated effort.
Highlights typosquatting, maintainer changes, suspicious package behavior, and bundle size impact.
Provides report, remediation, pull request, and CI monitoring templates for dependency work.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and sample implementations, not a complete built-in scanner.
Several playbook functions are illustrative and require project-specific implementation, credentials, error handling, and testing.
Vulnerability and version results depend on current external data and available audit tools.
License compatibility guidance is simplified and does not replace qualified legal review.

use_cases.title: Secure a Release
use_cases.description: Assess release dependencies, prioritize exploitable vulnerabilities, and define tested upgrade gates before deployment.

use_cases.title: Plan a Maintenance Backlog
use_cases.description: Rank outdated direct and transitive packages by security value, compatibility risk, age, and update effort.

use_cases.title: Review License Exposure
use_cases.description: Identify restrictive, incompatible, or unknown dependency licenses and prepare evidence for qualified legal review.

prompt_templates.title: Inventory Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository's dependency manifests. List direct and transitive dependencies by ecosystem, and identify missing lockfiles or unsupported formats.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Vulnerabilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the identified dependencies for known vulnerabilities. Rank findings by severity and exposure, then recommend the smallest safe upgrade for each issue.

prompt_templates.title: Review Licenses and Supply Chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess dependency licenses and supply chain signals for this project. Flag incompatible, unknown, suspicious, or abandoned packages with evidence and replacement options.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Staged Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged remediation plan for these audit findings. Include compatibility risks, test gates, rollback steps, pull request groups, and continuous monitoring.

output_examples.input: Review this Node.js lockfile and summarize dependency risk.
output: Risk summary: Two high-priority vulnerabilities affect runtime packages.
Priority action: Update the exposed authentication package after integration tests.
Follow-up: Review four transitive packages with unknown maintenance status.

output_examples.input: Check whether dependency licenses fit an Apache-2.0 project.
output: License review: Most dependencies use permissive licenses.
Review required: One package has an unknown license and two have additional obligations.
Next step: Confirm usage and distribution details with qualified legal counsel.

output_examples.input: Turn these scanner findings into a staged upgrade plan.
output: Stage one: Apply compatible security patches and run focused regression tests.
Stage two: Upgrade major versions separately with migration checks.
Stage three: Enable scheduled audits and assign ownership for remaining exceptions.

best_practices: Provide lockfiles, the project license, runtime exposure, and current scanner output before requesting analysis.
Confirm advisory data with authoritative scanners and package registries before approving remediation.
Apply upgrades in small reviewed groups with isolated branches, test gates, and complete rollback plans.
anti_patterns: Do not run forced upgrades across the repository without approval, compatibility review, and a clean rollback point.
Do not treat package age or name similarity as proof of vulnerability or malicious behavior.
Do not publish private package names, versions, or vulnerability details to external services without consent.

faq.question: Which dependency ecosystems are covered?
faq.answer: The playbook covers npm, Yarn, Python, Ruby, Java, Go, Rust, PHP, and .NET manifests. Some parsers require further implementation.

faq.question: Does the skill include a vulnerability scanner?
faq.answer: No. It guides authorized audit tools and provides sample integrations, but it does not ship a complete scanner or advisory database.

faq.question: Does dependency analysis require network access?
faq.answer: Current vulnerability, version, and size checks may query external services. Review privacy requirements before sending private package names or versions.

faq.question: Can it analyze transitive dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes, when complete lockfile or dependency-tree data is available. Manifest-only input may omit exact transitive versions.

faq.question: Will it automatically apply dependency upgrades?
faq.answer: It can propose commands and staged updates. Execute changes only with approval, isolated version control, tests, and a complete rollback plan.

faq.question: Are license conclusions legal advice?
faq.answer: No. The license checks are preliminary technical guidance and should be reviewed by qualified legal counsel.
